utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is case number IT-02-60-PT, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic, Dragan Obrenovic, Dragan Jokic and Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we have the appearances, please? Yes, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours, my name is Peter McCloskey and with me today are Anne Davis, Stacy de la Torre and Janet Stewart, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. On behalf of Mr. Blagojevic, I'm Michael Karnavas, counsel, and with me is Suzana Tomanovic, co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SLIJEPCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, I am Dusan Slijepcevic from Belgrade and I am representing the accused, Dragan Obrenovic. The lead counsel, Mr. Wilson, is not present today. I apologise on his behalf because he was not able to be with us this afternoon, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, I'm Miodrag Stojanovic, defender of the accused Dragan Jokic. Together with me today are Ms. Cynthia Sinatra as co-counsel, Chris Murphy as case manager and Dragoslav Djukic as interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Stefan Kirsch. I'm here on behalf of Mr. Nikolic and the co-counsel and I also apologise that the lead counsel, Mr. Londrovic is not present here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This Trial Chamber has received two motions for the absence of Mr. Obrenovic and the leading counsel as well as a written motion filed by the counsel of Nikolic. It says that it is his understanding from the decision not to attend the Pre-Trial Conference to be held this afternoon and to waive his appearance and the presence in the courtroom on this day. Those two motions are granted. We will proceed without the presence of the two accused and their leading counsels. In addition to the counsel, we notice that the Jokic team have a translator present in the courtroom to assist the lead and co-counsel in communicating with each other, as well as their clients. We have to remind the parties that interpreter should not be allowed to make any observation and intervention during the proceedings. And they should always bear in mind Rule 97 of lawyer and client privilege. Is that understood? I guess it's yes. Let me turn to the accused. Mr. Blagojevic, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about your health? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] It's not the best. Namely, I am undergoing therapy for high blood pressure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that this is a long case ahead of us so be careful of your health. Do you have anything to complain about? Do you have any special matters to bring to our attention at this moment? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. Your Honours, I would openly and clearly like to state here that I do not have a lawyer present here today who would represent me as my Defence counsel. I initiated this question a long time ago. However, things became a little complicated and due to a series of circumstances, wherein I was thwarted in different ways, I am forced to state this here and I would ask you kindly that the Chamber, as a guarantor and the protector of the rights of the accused also protect me in this sense. What I would like to say is that my lawyer, who introduced himself in that capacity has actually been dismissed by me and is no longer my Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm surprised to hear that. I have to draw your attention to the decision made by the Registrar dated the 8th of April, 2003, that your request has been dismissed and you did not make an appeal on that decision so the Registrar regards that decision is final. And at this stage, especially at the very start of a new trial, you still make such kind of observations. Do you have any specific reason for doing that? What is your specific request to this Trial Chamber? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] First, regarding the decision by the Registry, it did not pertain to this dismissal of my lawyer. It pertained to something regarding my Defence counsel and so on and so forth but that is not actually it. So the Registry did not find it fit to respond to me or to provide me with the opportunity in any way or to help me so that I could resolve the issue of the Defence counsel. Next, I think it is sufficient if I say that I absolutely have no longer any confidence in Mr. Karnavas and it would be a catastrophe for him to continue to represent me in this case and to defend me This can be substantiated in several ways but, please, do not exhaust me. I have the right to this and I would be the sorriest person on earth if I had to tell myself now that I should trust somebody that I'm not able to trust due to his actions to date. I am now very clear in this and you may -- what I'm saying now, I would like you to be aware of that and you can ask me to provide any kind of argumentation, and I have the arguments that I think that the trust that has been lost cannot be replaced, particularly in light of the events of the past year, especially since last July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think your Defence team has been working with you over a year and at this very moment, especially at the start of a new trial, you raise this issue to us, and I fail to see that there is any new reasons for your motion. If you stick to your original proposals, frankly speaking, I could tell you that your motion has been dismissed but if you have any new request or any new motion, we would like to hear from you. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] I would just like to ask you one thing, to make it possible for the gentleman not to be here to deal with the question of my Defence because he is unprepared for that and he is not going to do it. So in those terms, I am asking for assistance from this Chamber, if it is able to provide me with this assistance. Everything else is immaterial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, from Chamber's aspect, we see that your Defence team did a quite good job, if not the best. We are quite satisfied that your interests having safeguarded by this Defence team and we have no reason to change your Defence at this moment. Well, you may sit down. If you found some particular -- THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you permit me, Your Honours, please, what I have just said, I think I'm of sound mind, and I think that I really do know with what kind of values and things I am dealing with, and I think that I would like to be able to work in a normal, legal way. Please do not thwart me in this. Make it possible for me for somebody to represent me who would do that responsibly, legally, and properly. This lawyer here did not pass the test and I'm no longer interested in him. Please do not tell me that he should continue to represent me because he is really not able to do that. He has been dismissed and we can no longer go back on that. If there is some higher power to force things in this aspect, then that is something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Blagojevic, if you have some new requests apart from the original one, this Trial Chamber might consider to assign an independent counsel to help you draft a motion to bring the matter to our attention but if you stick to the original reasonings, I'm afraid that this case is closed. You may sit down, please. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jokic, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you understand? THE ACCUSED JOKIC: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: When did you arrive in The Hague from your provisional release? THE ACCUSED JOKIC: [Interpretation] I arrived on the 29th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready for the new trial? THE ACCUSED JOKIC: [Interpretation] Yes, I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have anything to complain about at this stage? THE ACCUSED JOKIC: [Interpretation] No, I do not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down. This Trial Chamber has noticed that Mr. Jokic arrived in the detention unit on the 29th of April, 2003, after the provisional release, and I will not ask the same questions concerning of the language issues to the accused every day but whenever there is a problem for you to follow the proceedings, please let me know. This is a Pre-Trial Conference held in accordance with Rule 73 bis and a decision made by the Pre-Trial Judge to discuss some specific matters with the aim to facilitate and prepare the case. By the order of the President, dated 1st April, 2003, this bench, the Trial Chamber I, section A is composed of three judges. Sitting on my right is His Excellency, Judge Vassylenko from Ukraine. Sitting on my right is Her Excellency, Judge Argibay from Argentina. My name is Liu, Daqun from China, the Presiding Judge of Trial Chamber I of the Tribunal. Frankly speaking, all of us have been sitting in at least one case before this Tribunal, which means that we are somehow familiar with the practice and the jurisprudence of this Tribunal. On the other hand, we are all from civil law legal systems and none of us from English-speaking countries. Since most of the counsels of both parties are from common law jurisdictions, there might be some frictions between judges and the parties in the future proceedings of this case. If this happens, we believe that the rule of the procedure and evidence of this Tribunal should prevail. If the both parties would like to use some specific practice or terminology during the proceedings, please be patient and explain to us. Today we have a very heavy agenda. There are several issues to be discussed, namely outstanding issues, outstanding motions, witnesses, exhibits, case presentation, and possibly any agreed facts. Let us begin with the easiest one, that is the case presentation. The first matter of the case presentation is the scheduling. I would like to draw the attention of all the parties to a decision we just rendered today, that this trial shall commence on Thursday, 8th May 2003 at 1415 hours in Courtroom III with the opening statement of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Prosecution, and we'll hear the first witness next Monday. The trial will commence on five-day-a-week schedule. The Trial Chamber may adjust its schedule as necessary due to witness-related issues, specific requests by the parties or other unforeseen circumstances. For instance, we may possibly reserve one day every second week to address any outstanding procedural issues or motions that may arise. We will inform the parties beforehand, with the aim for the proper arrangement of calling of the witnesses. If there is any short break, the Trial Chamber would like to advise the parties the schedule will be determined based on the length of witness's testimony and we will adjust it in accordance with the completion of witness testimony because we could not afford to have a witness under oath stay in The Hague for a quite long time so that to avoid any contaminations of that witness. At the same time, we are advised by the Registrar that each break between sittings should at least be 30 minutes. If we sit half day, each sitting will last about 70 minutes. If for a whole day, 90 minutes. Because we have more than one accused and a large Defence team in this case. The case will be heard in Courtroom III throughout the trial, I guess only this Trial Chamber could hold such a large team. There is a question I would like to address to both parties, that is the language of the proceedings. It seems to us that no member of the Prosecution or any of the Defence team use French. Do any of the parties object to not keeping a French transcript in this case? Of course, the audio tapes in French will still be available to any interested parties and as French is an official language of the Tribunal, simultaneous translation into French will still be available to anyone following the proceedings. All the decisions and judgements will still be translated into French. Any objections? Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. How about Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SLIJEPCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. So it has been decided that no French transcript will be available during the whole proceedings. As we have been advised that the Prosecution estimated its opening statement will be two or three hours, is that all right, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That is what we are planning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And your first witness will last for three sessions? And do you have any new suggestions as to the time for -- time frame for the first witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The first witness, as you know, testified at length in a previous trial and we have been able to cut down the number of exhibits and some of the time of his testimony from that trial so we are confident that the direct can be done within about three days. It's hard to come up with a more precise estimate than that but that's the counsel that has been dealing with Mr. Ruez tells me three days is doable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I have to tell you that the Defence team, the whole team, will have more or less, more or less, the same amount of time in their conducting of the cross-examination and there is also the time for you for re-examination, so probably the first witness will take about six days or seven days. Up to now we haven't received any indications on the exhibits you are going to tender through this witness. Are you going to file any list of exhibits concerning the first witness? I'm not asking you to file it right now but maybe before one or two days, you could file those exhibits. Particularly for the first witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, we have chosen those exhibits reduced down from the Krstic exhibits that he used and from some other exhibits and we should have hard copies available by the end of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we make it a rule that whenever you call a witness, one day or two days before, you should file that list of exhibits so that we could prepare which documents you are going to use during the direct examination of that witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As well as for the witness list, would you please file a list, at least one week in advance, for the witnesses you are going to call? Or any upcoming witnesses in two weeks or three weeks' notice. Of course that's subject to any changes which is unexpected.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. No problem. As you know, you have a list of the first 18 witnesses and we can continue to do that, no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. There are still some matters concerning with the Defence team. I understand that each Defence team will conduct its own cross-examination with one member of the team being responsible for objections and the cross-examination of witnesses. Cross-examination will follow the order of the indictment, unless due to the nature of the specific evidence given by the parties, the Defence team agree unanimously, to proceeds with a different order and inform the Trial Chamber of the changed order in advance. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SLIJEPCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is fine for us, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We have agreed to this at the last 65 ter conference and we do not have any further remarks on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I also agree to this procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. So it's settled. At this moment, this Trial Chamber would like to know again whether any accused will make a statement in accordance with Rule 84 bis. Mr. Blagojevic? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not able to do so right now because I have not agreed to defend myself. The lawyer who is present today as my Defence lawyer from the point in time when I dismissed it, I no longer recognise as my Defence attorney and whatever he says here is superfluous. If you allow me to choose a lawyer, then I will be able to proceed as usual with the usual procedure, but it would be very difficult for me to have to defend myself. It's something that I never considered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, from the Rules of Procedure I understand that you have the right to make a statement at any time during the proceedings. The particular question I'm going to ask you is that are you going to make a statement right after the opening statement delivered by the Prosecution? Could I guess that your answer is no at this moment? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, you may take it as that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Mr. Jokic? THE ACCUSED JOKIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not wish to make a statement after the Prosecutor's presentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Which does not mean that you will not make any statement during the whole proceedings, am I right? You may have that chance in the future. THE ACCUSED JOKIC: [Interpretation] Yes, if I decide so, I will notify you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Well, another issue is the outstanding motions. We have the 92 bis motions, 94 bis motions, but we prefer to defer the 92 bis motions at a later stage. Let's come to the 94 bis motions. The Prosecution's motion of 14 February, 2003, is currently under consideration by this Trial Chamber, and will be ruled in due course. At this moment, I would like to inform both parties that in the coming weeks, it may require additional oral submissions from the parties on experts in relation to the both 92 bis and 94 bis motions, and that they will be informed in advance of any such discussions. Another matter is the motion for leave to amend the witness list filed 17th April, 2003. Up to now, only one accused filed a response to this motion and was silent on the issue of the two additional witnesses. We understand that the motion seeks to add two witnesses, the witnesses has been identified by the Prosecution in the course of the investigations are therefore new. The Prosecution states in the motion that all the statements and information reports, relating to these witnesses have been disclosed to the Defence. Is that true, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sure it is, Your Honour. We don't have any reason to believe it's not, and we've received nothing new since this motion was filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. As no response has been received within the prescribed time frame, the Trial Chamber would like to grant the motion right now. It's granted. The next issue is the Prosecution's motion to supplement exhibit list filed on the 23rd April, 2003. Still there is no response from the accused, and the deadline for the response is the 7th of May. The motion seeks to add the following documents to the exhibit list: The first one, a video compilation, most of the videos already disclosed and identified. However the compilation has recently been complicated. The Prosecution states it has been disclosed to the Defence. Two, six video footage making up part of the video compilations referred to above. Motion does not state whether they are disclosed or not. Three, intercepts, dated July to October, 1995, obtained by SFOR. Motion does not state whether they are disclosed or not. Four, English translations of MUP documents added by the Trial Chamber's decision 20th March, 2003. Motion does not state whether they are disclosed or not. Logbook from Zvornik hospital obtained by the OTP in June, 2003. Motion does not state whether they are disclosed or not. Documents that will be relied on by the handwriting analyst. Motion does not state whether it is disclosed or not. The last piece is the two documents referred to by Butler in his updated military narrative. Motion does not state whether they are disclosed or not. Mr. McCloskey, would you explain for us whether they are -- all those documents have been properly disclosed to Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, they have, and counsel have had that material, each probably for a different amount of time, but we haven't had any real discovery problems thus far. Counsel has most of our material and we are continually -- in continual contact with them when we find that they don't have something. So as far as I know, they have all this material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At this moment, we would like to ask Defence counsel whether any of the Defence team would like to respond Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to this motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have received the disclosed material, we don't object to the Prosecution's motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SLIJEPCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we do not object to the motion either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, all these exhibits that the Prosecutor disclosed, we have received, and we do not object to their admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Your Honour the Defence for Mr. Nikolic has decided not to object to this motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Here I have to clarify one thing. We are not admitting those documents or materials into evidence at this moment. They have to be dealt with piece by piece when the case arrives. So as I understand that, the Defence counsel do not have the intention to respond and they do not have any objections for us to grant that motion from the Prosecution. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, Your Honour I have to say that I have not seen the SFOR intercept information although Mr. McCloskey and Ms. Stewart say that it has been disclosed. This is information that could be terribly relevant and decisive in Mr. Jokic's case and I'd like to have an extension of 24 hours or 48 hours to file a written motion deciding on whether we have any objections to the SFOR intercept information that Mr. McCloskey is discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that's reasonable. Mr. McCloskey, are you going to make some explanation on that? I just want to make sure whether this kind of material has been disclosed to the Defence counsel, especially for the Defence team of Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, absolutely been put in her locker, there is not much of significance that we could see, though they may find something significant, but they certainly had it for a while and I don't see any problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know Mr. McCloskey's definition of a while but we have had four large boxes of disclosure in the last few days and we have not had the opportunity to review all of the documents. If the Court would please just grant us an extension of a few days to make sure that these documents are not what they could possibly be as SFOR intercepts because part of our case is -- has to do with intercepts and it's very important to Mr. Jokic's Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you have to understand that as I said before, that we are not dealing with the admission of these documents into the evidence. We are just dealing with the motion filed by the Prosecution on that. Since the Prosecution said that the disclosure is completed, and there is no substantial, if I say, substantial objections to this motion, we will orally rule that the motion has been granted. Of course, at the same time, the Defence counsel of Mr. Jokic still have time to study and to do some research concerning those documents and if you have some problems with those documents, when the Prosecution are using those documents, you have the full opportunity to challenge their validity and reliability on that. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would prefer of course that the Court admit them subject to a response on the intercept information, but if they are admitted then we will write a formal motion challenging their authenticity and reliability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course you could do that. So we will rule that we will grant the motion from the Prosecution at this moment. Thank you very much for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The next issue is about the witnesses. How many witnesses are there on your list, Mr. McCloskey, in this case, the whole case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: About 149. And hopefully nothing more than in the 80s for actual witnesses, given the 92 bis law and other avenues at our disposal not to hear witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that's a large number, I must confess. But of course there will be some adjustments of the lists according to the decisions made by this Trial Chamber concerning the 92 bis and 94 bis motions, as well as the future developments of this case. And the Prosecution has already submitted a list of its intended first 18 witnesses on the 27th March, 2003, to the Defence and the Trial Chamber. Are there any changes concerning the first bunch of witnesses at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It appears (redacted)has refused to testify, so you can take her off the list. And for the rest of the list, nothing definitive at this time though we have been considering one of the witnesses as a possible 92 bis witness and we continue to try to see how we might be able to cut down the live witness list and see who may be available for 92 bis and that is a matter of ongoing efforts on our part in order to reduce this witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I appreciate very much your efforts in that direction. But if there is any changes of the witness lists, please inform us as well as the Defence team, as soon as possible so that we could prepare. The next issue is about the protective measures. Up to now, we notice that the Prosecution has not filed any motion for the protective measures for any witnesses at this stage. I believe that the Prosecution has been advised to file a motion for any of the first 18 witnesses for whom it will seek closed session or voice distortion, because of the logistic arrangements in this Tribunal only the request for the closed session or voice distortion need a motion. As for other witnesses, for their protective measures, the parties should have them indicated in the witness list and then raise it orally in the courtroom. The Chamber will make a ruling at the same time. Mr. McCloskey, are you going to file any motions concerning the protective measures or are you going to give us a new witness list indicating what kind of protective measures you request?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, right now we don't have -- the only witness that may require closed session got closed session in Krstic which as you recall was part of an ongoing order from the Court that we didn't need to make a motion for those witnesses. I don't see any others on this first list that we need closed session or voice distortion for. And I generally try to dissuade witnesses, for obvious reasons, we want public trials, if possible, without trying to over influence them. So on that matter of closed section and voice distortion I don't see that as a problem. A witness may come to me right before they testify and say something but I don't see that as a problem right now. As for pseudonym, this is something that is so subject, as I know Your Honours are familiar, is so subject to the last-minute changes of what is said to each other in the hotel room, and all, and how a person reacts to us when we see them a few days before, that I have not felt confident yet in -- to submit to the Court anything on these witnesses. Some we know from Krstic had pseudonyms and we shortly will be able to provide you with a list and our best estimates of what will involve in terms of pseudonyms but it's hard to say really until witnesses come here at the last moment but I think we can give you a pretty good estimate very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Another matter is the exhibits. Here I'm talking about those exhibits that are not currently on the exhibit list. I understand that during the proceedings, there might be some new exhibits appearing in the possession of the Prosecution or later on at the position of the Defence team but at least we need, at least, two weeks' notice about it, and the parties have to explain as to why the evidence has not been on the list and whether it would not be permitted at all. Is that agreeable to both parties that if there is any new evidence appeared, at least you will have two weeks notice beforehand? Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine, Mr. President, as you know there are lots of ongoing investigations and matters do arise and we will endeavour to get this material to the Defence as soon as possible and not use it in court before two weeks, before they have notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to try to avoid any preemptive attack by either parties to the other side so that the other party could make some research concerning those newly found materials. As for the tendering and the numbering of the procedures, are there any suggestions from the parties? Because different cases have different practices, you know. utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yes, we also go along with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Your Honours, on behalf of the Nikolic Defence team, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not 100 per cent in memory about it but I can tell you the agreed facts were very few, they didn't -- with four different Defence counsel, they really didn't provide much assistance in terms of your burden and duty, so we can provide you a report on what the very few agreed facts are but it hasn't -- it hasn't been much. utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. SLIJEPCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have already given our opinion, and we also submitted the text to the OTP in March this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we talked with the OTP on two occasions, with a view to trying to agree on some of the counts in the indictment and some issues relative -- related to the indictment. utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Your Honour, on behalf of Mr. Nikolic it is sorry to say that we are still in the same situation we have been in in the last Status Conference so to say that there are no agreed facts with our team. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Frankly speaking, I'm very disappointed on this issue. We also read the filings from the Defence team and in some filings the Defence team also mentioned, for instance, the armed conflict, the Srebrenica incidents, as well as the position of their clients, which might be constituted as the agreed facts. If there is any agreed facts between the parties, there is no need to prove it. So I appeal to both parties to work together once again to try to find out whether there is any agreed facts in this case so that, to facilitate the proceedings of this trial. But I'm not forcing our proposal at this stage on both parties. Yes, the next issue is the most complicated one, that is 92 bis witnesses. We have been seized with two motions filed by the Prosecution for 92 bis witnesses, the total number are 60 witnesses. This afternoon, the Trial Chamber will discuss two categories of witnesses with the parties, namely the Bosnian Muslim witnesses and the DutchBat witnesses. During the following proceedings, if one party feels that you need the private session at any time, please draw our attention to that, because we might touch upon some identities of the witnesses. Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, especially for the Bosnian Muslim witnesses, most of those are very likely to ask for pseudonyms. I know from my experience it's hard to tell which ones so if we do start discussing the Bosnian Muslim witnesses, it would be a good idea to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. But if we use the agreed pseudonym at this stage, is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we have a -- if everyone is sure of what the agreed pseudonym is that may take us a bit to get our heads together a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: For instance, I would like to draw your attention to the Witness W41. Do you understand whom I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The defence team?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure because I think W41 was a notation from the Krstic trial and the Prosecutor is now marking their protected witnesses as P with a number after it. So we have a pseudonym list that has the Prosecutor's notation on it as P- a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, W41 is the 65 ter number. Am I right? Because we used this kind of pseudonym just to facilitate discussions rather than the true pseudonym in the proceedings, as I understand. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think I know who you're talking about, but again, this is -- and the Krstic case of course complicated that because they all have pseudonyms and numbers. It may take us a minute off the record just to get on the same sheet, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let us refer to the witness as W41 in accordance with the 65 ter filings. Is that okay? As for this witness, we do not think it's necessary for this person to remain the witness on the witness list, because we believe that W62 and W63 are testifying on the same topic. Why are three witnesses necessary, especially since 92 bis statement would need to be taken? Mr. McCloskey, can you give us an explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This witness is from one of the three only-known survivors of the Kravica warehouse massacre where some 500 to a thousand people were killed. It is the single-most massacre in the Bratunac zone of responsibility and as such we thought a third written account of this incident would assist the Chamber. We did not think it was worth another live witness but we did think a third written account would assist you. One of the issues that will be perhaps discussed over the Kravica warehouse was whether or not this was part of a systematic and organised execution or whether it was an initial detention site that -- where a fight broke out and prisoners were killed in response to something a prisoner did to a guard. That's an important issue and the overall command and control issues of the case, and we thought perhaps a third witness might help you in that decision. I agree with Your Honour, it's not absolutely necessary, but we thought as a written 92 bis document, that it would not overly burden the resources of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will hear from the Defence counsel on this particular witness. Generally speaking, we don't need so many witnesses to testify on the same issue, on the same matter, unless there are some particular reasons for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if the witness isn't necessary to testify in a matter that because he has he or she has nothing to offer, in addition to what has been offered by other witnesses, then I dare say that witness, the testimony of the witness is cumulative and there is no need to introduce that witness at all, whether it be by as a live witness or as a statement. This particular witness, if you -- if I understand, Mr. McCloskey correctly, and I believe I do, he believes this incident is quite significant to his case and this is a quite significant witness and he's going to use this statement as a basis for confirming what the other two witnesses have said, either the witness is cumulative in which event he should not be heard or if he's important, he should be brought in subject to cross-examination, just like the other two witnesses. Otherwise, it tends to have a cumulative effect. It doesn't assist the Defence in any way because we are unable to cross-examine that particular witness, all it does is confirm what other witnesses have said about a very important incident so we do believe that it's an infringement on Mr. Blagojevic's right under Article 21 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any other observations from the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. SLIJEPCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we don't have any remarks on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have a list of witnesses here with the markings that were used. This is the most recent list of witnesses that we received from the Prosecution. utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to agree with Mr. Karnavas and Mr. -- what was said on behalf of Defence for Mr. Obrenovic, as you read in our written motion, our concern is also that either a witness is very important to the case and then we should be provided with the right to cross-examine that witness or it might not be necessary at all to bring in the statement, the written statement, according to 92 bis. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are not going to make any rulings concerning those witnesses. We are just going to hear from those parties their views on that issue. utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm really sorry but we have no markings showing the witnesses that you're referring to. If the Trial Chamber would like, I can offer my copy of our latest list of pseudonyms that was provided by the Prosecution and we can coordinate so that we can -- if the usher would like to provide it to the Trial Chamber maybe we can come to some kind of conclusion as to who we are talking about so we are all in understanding about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As I said before, those pseudonyms are for the trial proceedings at a later stage. utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, I have to apologise. utterances.text: In the office, yes. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.text: We have given one copy to Ms. Sinatra. We can get Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. another copy for counsel very quickly.

utterances.text: Can we make a break here? Because I think it will take sometime. So we will resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sinatra, have you got the 65 ter filings?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think we are on the same page now, thank you.

utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Kirsch how about you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honour, I've been provided with them.

utterances.text: Thank you very much. So we will proceed. The next three witnesses are: W49, W52 and W54. We understand these three witnesses are Potocari witnesses. utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, as you know, I don't think it's necessary for them to come to court and testify. However, they are -- they all have testified in Krstic, there is a nice written record of their testimony and their cross-examination. Potocari is a two-day period, a very difficult and complex situation that we dealt with very thoroughly in the previous trial. We didn't feel a need to put on that many witnesses at this trial but we did want to put on the witnesses that had been cross-examined and had provided credible testimony at Krstic as a reference, and to add to the overall case as we needed to prove it. What was going on there? What was their attitude? The forcible transfer issue is very important, and each individual had something to offer, we felt, as witnesses, but they didn't go to the particular acts or conduct of the accused so I think this does help the trier of fact see the overall picture which was a difficult and complex period of time, and I don't think it's -- it creates any really undue burden or difficulty because it would be 92 bis, and I would point out that 92 bis itself is designed to introduce evidence of a -- that's cumulative. That's one of the factors. It's not one of the reasons why you shouldn't be 92 bis, it's one of the reasons why you should be, unlike what counsel said. So we do think that this helps you. We don't think it's a big burden and we can also, I think, way back when, Judge Hunt suggested that we highlight matters from the transcript that we thought was particularly important which we can do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any response from Defence team? If you just repeat whatever you said with the previous witnesses, I think this Trial Chamber have already taken note but if you have any particular request, you may raise at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nothing at this time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU

utterances.speaker: MR. SLIJEPCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we have nothing, Your Honour.
