utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe these witnesses, if they are going to introduce the statement, the negotiation that happened in prior cases was that if they introduced the statement because during that trial they were allowed to be cross-examined based on the facts of that case. Krstic only took into consideration the Bratunac Brigade and the area of Srebrenica, now Mr. Jokic is charged with this area from the Zvornik Brigade and even if the witness is only asked a few questions relative to the Zvornik Brigade I believe that these witnesses need to be questioned since that is a major part of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kirsch?

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is nothing to add at this moment, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Next witness is W57. It seems to us that the statement of this witness was very brief and it's very general. This statement was provided by the MUP in August, 1995. We wonder whether there is any additional OTP statement at this stage. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Not at this time, Mr. President. At the time we filed this motion, well, it was last February, and we were in a perfect world hoping to get results back a little earlier and so based on those results, we would have made a more thorough interview but we can see from this MUP interview that this is a very important survivor for an important incident that occurred, that is reflected in the reports of the Bratunac Brigade. I can go into some detail on that if you'd like. I'll try to make it brief. But there is a report, I believe it's dated 17 July, where -- of the Bratunac Brigade, where they identify capturing four children and that those children should be brought for propaganda purposes and filmed because they say Muslims are killing themselves. This person is one of those four children, and we have identified one of the other children as a testimonial witness but only one, and so we thought that a more thorough 92 bis statement of this witness would help corroborate, help back up this important witness that would be testifying, yet would not take up the Court's time regarding this very important issue. It's important because the witness that will testify identifies Muslim adults that were captured with him that are now on the missing list, presumed murdered, and so that is an important incident. It's one of the few documented incidents that we have left over from the documents of the Bratunac Brigade who we know cleansed their documents of most incriminating things so given that it is reflected in the documents, we have two witnesses that could help the Court greatly. This would help corroborate the one that actually testifies but you are correct, it is only a MUP statement and we would definitely have a more thorough ICTY statement prior to offering a 92 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm not going into the details about the statement but could you please tell me how old was he when the incidents happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think about 16. These were teenagers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's not children but teenagers; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The document of 17 July makes a reference to children, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I perhaps shouldn't quote Bratunac Brigade documents but I have children in my translation so -- but we do have their dates of birth and I think teenagers is what they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any special response from the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecutor used the word "important" several times. He also indicated in his own personal belief that this was for propaganda purposes whatever the motive was to have these children filmed and also he made references to documents being cleansed by the Bratunac Brigade. I'm unaware of any evidence being cleansed. This is news to me. I trust we will find out soon enough from the Prosecution. However, if the Prosecutor believes that this witness is important, then that witness should come in to be cross-examined. There is -- I mean it's very clear that Mr. Blagojevic, as all the other accused, have the right to confront the witnesses, and what they are trying to do here is produce one witness and then through other witnesses try to bolster the testimony and validate and verify the testimony of other witnesses, and that is totally improper because it denies the accused the opportunity to cross-examine the witness. If the witness has nothing to add, then the witness should not be here, either to testify or a statement should not come in but some minor statement that a witness may have given to MUP, I believe, is totally improper without the witness coming in to be subjected to cross-examination, particularly in light of the age of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. SLIJEPCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I absolutely support Mr. Karnavas's stand on this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we support Mr. Karnavas's stand on this point, on behalf of Mr. Blagojevic, but also we believe that maybe the introduction of this evidence is totally unnecessary because I can assure this Trial Chamber that Mr. Jokic is not asserting or does not believe or does not have a theory that any of the Muslims killed themselves. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kirsch?

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Your Honour, although I agree with everything that was said by my learned friends I want to draw the attention of this Honourable Trial Chamber to another point and to let me clarify this. This more or less adversarial surrounding I'm facing here I'm coming from Germany from an inquisitorial system but I have to get used to it this -- the point I want to bring your attention to is that even if the witness is a witness for the Prosecution, there might be something in the testimony which is mitigating, which is helping my client maybe, and therefore I think all witnesses are witnesses for the truth, and if they are brought in 92 bis and without any possibility to cross-examine them, then I really have no means to find out maybe mitigating circumstances with these witnesses and so our argument in the written motion that there is a need to cross-examination is also relied on this necessity to find out maybe mitigating circumstances or circumstances which are good for my client. Please reconsider that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think that's the very reason that we ask for your views on the particular witnesses in the 92 bis filings. And the -- but at the same time, we also think that you have that opportunity to read the statement of that witness and to see whether there is any mitigating facts in his statement, and we'll see what should we do at a later stage. The next witness is about Witness W61. In light of other witnesses and especially with the W60 witness, is it necessary to call this witness? Or is it just repetitive? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this witness -- I'm sure you're aware there is a famous videotape dated 13 July, that depicts many of the events that occurred in Potocari and along the road between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje. This witness is depicted in that video as a child coming out of the woods in a line of soldiers, and it is from July, 1995. He's now an adult. But his testimony is particularly important in that it corroborates the video, it shows that he talks about what happened there did in fact happen, he is a historical witness in that regard and his story about what happened along the road is different from his brother's, who is the other witness you point out. In his story, he sneaks off to get water. He's told to go off and get water, and when he does that, he sneaks on to a bus and crawls under the dress of a woman and is able to escape. His brother, who is the actual witness we would like to call, is sitting in this large meadow when the Serbs announce that anyone born at a certain time should stand up and would be allowed to leave. This person was too old, based on that year of birth, but the evidence will show that an older man next to him said, "Stand up son, stand up." So he stood up Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and was able to be let go with the younger children and teenagers. This is a critical story to show you that the mass -- the organised, mass execution process is still in place, is still working just like it happened in Potocari where men of the same age were being separated. Part of the theme and theory of our case will be that the thousand men that were separated at Potocari is part of the process of the 6.000 men that were detained along the road, and we show you that the process is in place taking their property, destroying their IDs, not giving them food, giving them only a little bit of water, particular-age men being chosen, that they are identical. That shows you that the process is the same. It's part of the same murder operation. This one witness is important for that. He does help establish that because he is allowed to go free as a young man, as part of an organised operation. There is some other evidence in the record of that but that on such an important point, we thought it would be necessary for you to hear that one witness live but that his younger brother, who is in the record, cross-examined on the video, and has his own story of escape is something that is of historical importance and legal and evidentiary importance for you to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any response from the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I guess there is none. The next --

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. I was waiting for the response there. I just would like to ask the Court. I know this is a Pre-Trial hearing and it's kind of similar to an opening statement with Mr. McCloskey referring to murder operations. This is the point where the accused is presumed innocent and nothing has been proven yet and I ask that a motion in limine be instigated to prevent him from using terms at the Pre-Trial hearing. They are usable at the opening statement but those things are not proven yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the Prosecution got special permission from this Trial Chamber to present somehow part of the matters which is related to whether it's necessary to have this witness or not. There need to be some explanations from the Prosecution's side and I guess at this stage, it's just one-sided allegations. It's not the facts. The Prosecution used certain terms just to facilitate the procedures. Now we are dealing with only the procedural matters rather than substantial matters. That's why I try my best to refrain from going into the details of certain incidents. Yes, Mr. Kirsch, do you have any response?

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: No response, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. The next witness is W65. I think the situation is the same with the previous one, that we have the W64 and W66. It seems to me that it's quite cumulative. Is it necessary? Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, we believe it would assist the Court in its evaluation, Your Honour. The murders at Orahovac are of significant importance to the case. They are the first known organised mass executions that occur in the Zvornik Brigade zone of responsibility. Four people survived them. We have provided you a means to see the testimony of -- or the information of three. One that has testified that is particularly important that is not yet the subject of discussion, that being number 64, Witness P108, but number 65 previously testified and was cross-examined, so we have a credible record of this witness's experience in what is a significant event, only one of some four or five like this, and again, it's a transcript that is reliable and gives you an account of an important event, and in addition, we hope the first time to provide some Serb witnesses to this account, so having another Muslim witness on the record will help you sort out whether or not the Serb witness is telling the truth which will be your burden because it will be difficult but we do think those Serb witnesses will help you determine what the truth is, but it will be more difficult, as I'll explain later in a more appropriate forum. Also, it's important to remember that the survivor witnesses that survived the large mass executions, Orahovac, the Petkovci dam, the Pilica area, Branjevo farm, these witnesses also started off either in Potocari or as detainees along the road, and all spent the night of the 12th and 13th in the Bratunac zone and all have testimony directly related to the horrendous things that occurred to them in Bratunac, and since we have the commander of the Bratunac Brigade at trial, at this trial, the Prosecution will pay particular attention to some of the incidents that occurred in Bratunac. We did at the Krstic trial but we will even more so at this trial since we do have the actual commander. So it's not just the final mass execution that these -- that this man was involved in, it's also his experience as he was held in Bratunac or in -- nearby. That is also one of the reasons why his evidence is important. And I should point out that the person that this affects most is accused Obrenovic, who has not objected to this witness, though it does also affect Mr. Jokic because Orahovac is involved in Mr. Jokic's case as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any response?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We don't object, Your Honour. However, I guess I do have a minor problem with some of the characterisations made by Mr. McCloskey when he talks about a credible record and reliability. I just want to make sure that I'm on the record in stating that simply because somebody has testified in a previous trial, and may have been cross-examined, doesn't necessarily mean that that witness would have been cross-examined in the same way in which we would prefer to have that individual cross-examined. So while I do not object to this particular witness, although I do think it's -- it is somewhat cumulative, I would -- I don't want to give the impression that by doing so, at least with other witnesses I am conceding that statements taken or transcripts from previous trials are necessarily credible records or the testimony reliable. I think it's a case-by-case base, witness by witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your statement is in the record. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. SLIJEPCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there is just one thing we would like to add on behalf of Mr. Dragan Obrenovic, namely that witness is testifying about Orahovac and will still stand by our motion of the 7th of April, 2003, in relation to this business too, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that I would just like to make a blanket statement that we already have on the record in our motion that every -- each and every one of the witnesses that the Prosecution is trying to introduce under 92 bis, A and D, and 94 bis, we -- if they are cumulative, then the Prosecution shouldn't be bringing them -- their evidence forward. But if the Prosecution wishes to introduce transcripts or statements or exhibits without our ability to cross-examine, then it violates Mr. Jokic's rights and every one of these, because of the joint criminal enterprise, applies to the acts and conducts of the accused as charged in the indictment. And I would just like that to be a standing objection with every witness so we don't have to do it each time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Kirsch?

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is nothing to add to what I said previously, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The next witness is W71. We found that statement of this witness is not detailed enough so I wonder whether it's necessary to keep it on the witness list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is much like the other witness that you pointed out where the statement was not as perhaps detailed as some of our normal statements, and my argument is similar. This is a -- the Branjevo Military Farm massacre, perhaps the biggest massacre of this incident, and we have the testimony of two survivors. He is the third. We thought, having this survivor's voice be heard and his evidence be heard, what happened to him in Bratunac, what happened to him at the farm, would assist you in both those important areas, both in Bratunac and what happened at the Branjevo farm and as a result we were going to take a more detailed statement and provide that under 92 bis, if so allowed. And if I could make one comment on the law, the Galic appeals case says basically that only where the evidence goes to direct participation in a joint criminal enterprise does 92 bis become a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any specific points that Defence teams would like to make concerning this witness? Yes, Ms. Sinatra?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just in response to the legal argument that Mr. McCloskey just put forward, the Galic case not only stands for the acts and conducts of the accused but if it is a challenge to the mens rea which they are charging Mr. Jokic with knowledge or proof of the knowledge of the individual, then it does fall under acts and conducts of the accused and it should not be allowed to be presented without cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this moment, we are not arguing about the legal issues and interpretations of any previous judgements. We are concerned with the particular witness. Do you have any objections concerning this particular witness? This is what we want to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: We have an objection to every witness that they want to introduce, the statement, the transcript or the exhibit, because we want the right to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So there is no specific points that you would like to make concerning this particular witness, am I right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would not like for them to come testify at all or have evidence presented but if it is presented we would like to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there is some additional witnesses whom the Trial Chamber may propose 92 bis or recommend be deleted from the witness list. The first two are Witness 45 and 46. In the 65 ter summaries, the Prosecution has indicated that if the witness W45 testified, W46 will not be called. And currently both witnesses are on the list of the first 18 witnesses. Therefore, we would like to raise this issue at this Pre-Trial Conference. We need an explanation from the Prosecution side. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We have been able to resolve this problem, Your Honour, and Witness 46 is -- has refused to testify, and Witness 45 provides some very important evidence. So we are only asking for one of those. I mentioned that earlier but of course it's impossible to tell which people I was talking about, but that is one of the first 18 witnesses that we have withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And Witness 55 and 56, we wonder why their testimony is necessary from both witnesses, because of course the both witnesses are on the first 18 witness list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are attempting to resolve which witness should be best but it's a situation where they both recall certain things and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. they may need -- their testimony may not have any meaning unless it's seen together. This is an odd situation that we occasionally find ourselves in and we are usually able to sort it out prior to testimony, but out of an abundance of caution in case we find ourselves in a situation where one witness's meaning would not have any meaning without the other we put them both down. We should be able to resolve these witnesses very soon, Your Honour. We are working on it because we have identified the problem you have identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Another one is W76 witness. We wonder whether we could have this witness's testimony into the Rule 92 bis statement witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, in my review of -- in getting ready for this hearing today, I came to a similar conclusion, but with a slight twist. This witness was particularly compelling in showing the trauma and the effect on the Muslim female population of being separated from their family and what we would ask is that we be allowed to play ten or 15 minutes of this witness's testimony, an edited version so it's just the important parts at the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. The next witness is W77 and W78. Is it necessary for both witnesses to testify? Or maybe you may select among them one for the live testimony and the other for the 92 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's what our intention was. We at this stage put them both on because we needed to do a little more research on which would be the most appropriate live witness, but for the reasons you state, we would be only asking for one of those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Next column of witnesses are DutchBat witnesses. Could I draw your attention to the witness W33? We understand that there will be a lot of soldiers to testify what happened there. I wonder whether there is any additional transcript that the party and the Chamber should have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Koster may have testified at the Rule 61 hearing, Your Honour, and that would be something that we should add to the 92 bis if we have not already, though we are not sure at this point whether we gave you -- when I say the Rule 61 hearing, that was a long time ago. We used to put on hearings in order to obtain charges, and there were a few Srebrenica witnesses put on in public by the Prosecution, and Mr. Koster was one of them because of what he witnessed. He was also called back as a witness in Krstic because he was a lieutenant that was in charge at a particular time and was able to testify about the freedom of movement between Srebrenica and Potocari on the 11th of July which became an important issue in the Krstic case. It's not clear at this time whether that will be an important issue in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The next witness is W36 witness. We wonder is it necessary for him to give the testimony because we found that the statement is quite cumulative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, this -- all we wanted was his trial testimony from Krstic, and my recollection of this witness is that he -- I'm sorry, I'm wrong on that. [Prosecution counsel confer].

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The reason we've put him on, Your Honour, is because he's one of the few Dutch witnesses that talks about the approach into Srebrenica and the damage that was being done by the troops, to show you that there is a reason why the populace was leaving. That was something we felt needed to be addressed in our evidence and so that's why we put him on there, though it wasn't a huge point, it was a -- something to help make your job easier and probably something that wouldn't be hotly contested by the Defence so that is why that particular witness is there, to establish the -- what was happening to the area around Srebrenica as the troops approached and took it over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The next witness is W34. It's on the witness list and is it possible to have this witness to be a 92 bis witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we -- our records show that he is a 92 bis witness, not a testimonial witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. I see. And how about W29 witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this particular Dutch soldier is important because he tries to follow some Muslim -- some buses with Muslim men in them and when he gets to Bratunac, he gets stopped, his vehicle gets stolen and he is able to show that there was an organised effort to prevent the Dutch in Bratunac, right near the headquarters of Mr. Blagojevic, there was an organised effort to cut off the Dutch's eyes and ears. This is an important piece of evidence. It was at the Krstic trial. It will be at this trial, and I imagine it will be something that Mr. Karnavas would like to have a chance to cross-examine on, and I think it's important evidence for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And W37 witness? Is it the same situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He is a 92 bis witness, not as important as the previous witness, and he is a 92 bis witness. We felt he was important because he does see truck loads of corpses along the road and is one of the few witnesses that actually sees that but we felt, since he couldn't tie in the act or conduct of any accused and didn't know who killed those people, that it would be appropriate for 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about W38 witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Same thing. This is a 92 bis witness. His unique story is that he is able to provide evidence of ethnic cleansing by a police dog unit or excuse me a dog unit. It's not exactly clear which unit owns the dogs but he is able to see a bloody German shepherd dog that is with a group of Serb soldiers and he hears a rather compelling account from how that dog got bloody, and it's consistent with the overall theme of our case and it is not necessary for you to see that as live evidence but I think it's an important element of the case. We now, from new video see German shepherd dogs present in Potocari so this new video will corroborate this account and I think make your job easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I want to make a clarification about the statement of this witness. To confirm that Major Nikolic mentioned by this witness is not the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, now that you point out to me, that probably is the same Nikolic, though he just sees him around and there is no particular acts or conduct that would be criminal in nature and so we are really not asking you to consider that, and that could be redacted if that was a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I believe that is all for these two columns of witnesses. Of course, we will hold such kind of hearings at a later stage, whenever we have a chance, and this Trial Chamber will inform both parties, if necessary, and when and how to conduct this kind of hearing concerning the 92 bis and 94 witnesses. Are there any particular matters that both parties would like to raise to this Trial Chamber? Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to have a chance to consider the comments of Mr. Blagojevic and discuss that with the Prosecutor. This is an issue that is of concern. Again you asked us to talk to you when our backgrounds tended to be different. In my common law background, which I come from, this is an issue that has several ways of being dealt with. I know I am here and I want to deal with it the proper way that it should be dealt with here but I would ask the Court to allow us to take more consideration on this issue, and perhaps provide the Court with some kind of filing. One of the problems that I would -- I don't have an answer to, is that I'm aware of an ethical code that the Defence counsel has and it says something about if the -- obliging the counsel to withdraw if the client loses confidence. There also could be a situation where a legal ruling is made by the Court and the counsel for an accused has a conflict of interest in appealing that legal ruling and who is to protect the rights of the accused to appeal a legal ruling where that appeal would be in conflict with the counsel's position? These are some of the legal entanglements that are of concern and I would just like to have a chance to think about them and discuss them with my superiors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Anything else from the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to briefly respond to that. I think a couple of things should be mentioned on the record. One, a junior Prosecutor calling me and insisting that I try to find another co-counsel which I thought was pretty unprofessional and pretty unnecessary, so I think that that has to be on the record. Secondly, I'm unaware of any ethical rule that obliges me to withdraw if a particular client loses confidence. Under my rule -- ethical code, and I've spent the better part of my career as a court-appointed lawyer in the United States, both on the federal side and on the state side, I take my guidance from the Trial Chamber, from the judges. It is the Judge who will allow me to withdraw from the case. Normally under these circumstances I'm asked one question and that is am I prepared to go forward to trial? Have I prepared the case? In this instance we have prepared. This is an unusual situation. Obviously, the Rules allow Mr. Blagojevic to represent himself. Frankly, he's not capable of doing that. That's my professional opinion. He does need legal representation. If the Trial Chamber feels that I or Ms. Tomanovic or both of us should be withdrawn from the case, we will do so but we will take our directions from the Trial Chamber. So I don't want to make any self-serving statements at this point. I'm not trying to stay in, I'm not trying to get -- to withdraw. We have been working on this case from day 1, with the expectation that we would be going to trial, also with the expectation that at any moment the Trial Chamber, for whatever reason, could decide to have us withdraw from the case, so we will do whatever the Trial Chamber decides in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any response or anything to add by Mr. Blagojevic at this stage? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that the situation is crystal clear. Here, the lawyer has mentioned ethics, and the attitude to ethics. I really do not have to look for any other words or waste my nerves or my health which is not good any way. I really need somebody who will work professionally, independently, and so on and so forth, and I don't need someone who will threaten my mental and -- the state of my mental and physical health even before we reach the main problem, that is before the main problem is resolved. For more than a month, I have had no communication with the mentioned gentleman, nor does he find any possibility to show that he's interested in what I'm saying now. All that is being said here about the -- about documents, about the evidence, and it is very important that I have a look at it and read it, and therefore to look at it from my point of view and determine my position towards all that, all this has been blocked. I am completely unaware that it exists and therefore what purpose does it serve? What he knows and what he said here on a couple of occasions when he rose up and spoke, I think is a story which isn't of much help to me. The general situation is of no help to me. It is concrete matters that are of help to me, and when we come to them, and when they are up for solution, then it will be too late. Please understand me, responsibly, if you conclude to the contrary that I'm not responsible, that I am fabricating something or trying to manipulate something, you've got the law and therefore you can apply any measures against me, but any other option except Mr. Karnavas's Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. immediate withdrawal from the case is out of the question, because he has betrayed my confidence fully. He has let me down completely and showed that we cannot succeed and he has done that in a very unusual way. And this opened my eyes. And although I do not know much about law because I know what I needed in my profession, however, it opened my eyes and I realised how things are really done in situations like this. I'm not trying to dodge responsibility and I'm saying I do not want to defend myself. No. It would be insane if I did that, but a lawyer of my choice must professionally represent my interests or he cannot be my lawyer. If I am to place my trust in -- if I place my trust in someone and then he starts manipulating it, then well, the gentleman says he does not respect any ethics, that he's not familiar with that, and that he does not want to discuss it at all, I believe he said it all when he said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may sit down, please. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The jurisdiction of this Tribunal, as well as the practice of this Tribunal are quite different from any domestic jurisdictions, I must confess. In the assignment of the counsel, the Chamber has limited influence and power to do that. It may rest upon the Registrar to do that. And I think at this moment, we have to identify the issues: What is the problem here? Still, I'm a little bit confused. If Mr. Blagojevic raised the issue of replacement of the counsel at this stage, all I could say is that this matter is over, because the Registrar has already made a decision to this effect. And the Defence has the opportunity to appeal to this decision but he did not. So the Registrar regards this decision is final and his Defence team will go on forward with the Defence in the following proceedings. The second issue is that whether there is new issue raised by Mr. Blagojevic at this stage. That is to represent himself. If he wants to represent himself, without the help from his legal counsel, we should have the motion which will stipulate the reason for doing that at this stage of the time. In the practice of this Tribunal, to be specific in the Milosevic case, the accused decided to represent himself at the very beginning of his arrival in this Tribunal, but the situation is a little bit different. If Mr. Blagojevic wants to represent himself at this stage, we would like to see what kind of reason is found in this motion. Mr. Blagojevic, are you prepared to submit a motion to this effect? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I feel I must say something and say it very clearly. This decision, if I may call it that, of the Registry which you have just mentioned has absolutely nothing to do with my decision to fire this lawyer. It has to do with something completely different, because, please, if that decision is relevant, then I really don't know what to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Blagojevic, I'm asking you a question. You just answer this question so we could make a decision towards your request. We are not talking about whether this decision is valid or not. We are not talking about the reasoning behind that decision. We just want to identify what is your request so that we could make a decision. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am requesting that, in accordance with the Rules, that I be allowed a lawyer of my choice, who will, based on the rights that are guaranteed to me, that is my fundamental rights, I ask that I be allowed a lawyer who will defend my interests in the interests of justice and truth, and the lawyer that I have at the moment cannot do that. As I have said, I won't repeat it, I don't want to look like a parrot, I simply do not trust him any longer and all that you are doing now and that you are imposing on me the decisions that he will continue to represent me, is disastrous for my standing here, and if that is the objective, then I'm really at a loss for words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Blagojevic, I think this matter has been dealt with for many, many times. The Pre-Trial Judge granted you two hearings concerning this matter. The Registrar made a decision to this effect already. You are allowed the opportunity to appeal on those decisions. If you repeat the same reasonings you mentioned before in your motion, I'm afraid to rule that this matter is over. But any way, if you want to make any new request, we would like to entertain it. You understand that? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there is no need to disregard what I have done so far and to disregard the moves that I have made so far. This should not be disqualified. I still would like to state again, as far as my to-date lawyer is concerned, the situation is quite clear. I fired him. I do not permit him to be involved in my case. Any involvement of his in my case is a catastrophe for me, does not lead to a resolution of this but is detrimental for me. So please, I'm asking you to understand, I don't know what else I can say. I don't know what new reasons you would like to hear from me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that we are talking about different matters. In this case, we will entrust the Registrar to assign to you an independent counsel to consult with you on this very matter. We couldn't debate in this courtroom for a very long time. If you don't trust your Defence team on this particular matter, I think an independent counsel will talk to you about all those matters. And then if you file a motion -- if you want to file a motion, that independent counsel could help you in this aspect, and we'll see what shall we do to this motion, but in the meantime, if there is no extraordinary reason to overthrow the decisions made by the Registrar, I think your present Defence team will still work with you in your case. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] I do not accept that. And I absolutely refuse any further involvement of them, because that is dangerous for me in my situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, talk to that independent counsel about this and discuss with him. Anyway, our case will start on Thursday afternoon. There is no other reason to delay the starting of this case. You may sit down, please. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess that is all for today's Pre-Trial Conference. We will see you in the opening statement. That is on Thursday afternoon, 2.15, in the same courtroom. See you there. We will rise.

procedural_notes.text: [The accused Obrenovic and Nikolic not present]
